metadata.title: Works On My Machine
metadata.purpose: Provenance Gatekeeper development log, Week 1 — the infrastructure that has to exist before any AI verification: Docker isolation, canonically promoted manifests, and a CI/CD gate that physically blocks unverified code.
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Hindi, one word. Wagwan rule is Bear-only and does not apply to this channel.
metadata.audience: Humanitarians AI fellows and practitioners following the Provenance Gatekeeper build
metadata.source: Week 1: Infrastructure & CI/CD — Video Script, Provenance Gatekeeper Development Log. 5-scene cut (HOOK / FRAMEWORK / WORKED EXAMPLE / FALSIFIABILITY / SCAFFOLDED TASK). Supplied 2026-09-15; PR corrected to #44 and dual render added by the author in the same revision.
metadata.dual_render: 16:9 master + 9:16 companion, BOTH EXPLICITLY REQUIRED by the script, which also asks to keep core visual artifacts centre-framed for 9:16 safe zones. Every pattern here has a registered <Pattern>916 variant and CiGateSplit / ThreeStageBand both RE-LAY OUT for portrait (panels stack, band serializes top-to-bottom) rather than cropping. 9:16 is a different beat sheet, never a crop — RENDER-TARGETS.md §3. Derive with ./art vertical.
metadata.color_semantics: Claude FIDELITY skin — cream #FAF9F5 / stage #F2F0E9, warm ink #3D3929, terracotta #D97757 as the ONE accent. The source script specifies the dark Brutalist palette with a red accent; a claude-explainer may not be retinted (CLAUDE-BRAND.md). Terracotta carries every 'red' the script asks for: the WORKS ON MY MACHINE snap, the struck-through CI/CD axis, the armed merge button. Structural intent — visible grid, exposed labels, zero border-radius, hard cuts — is preserved.
metadata.channel_note: Narrated in the FIRST PERSON by Onkar Bhujbal, matching the script's own Scene 1 VO. The Kokoro am_onyx voice is a synthetic read of Onkar's own script, not a clone of his voice.

beats.narration_text: I am Onkar Bhujbal, a software engineer. Works on my machine is the death of microservices. My project is the Provenance Gatekeeper, and before we write a single line of A.I. verification, we have to guarantee the environment never drifts.

beats.narration_text: We evaluate infrastructure against the Zero-Drift Matrix. One: is the execution isolated? Two: are the manifests automatically promoted? Three: does the repository physically block unverified code? If a pipeline fails one of these axes, your deployment is a liability.
beats.new_visual_element: The Zero-Drift Matrix — three axes, lit in narration order

connector draws; panel 02 CANONICAL MANIFEST lights on 'Two'
connector draws; panel 03 CI/CD GATE lights on 'Three' and holds
mono line lands under the band: fail one axis = liability

beats.narration_text: Here is the matrix applied to week one. We scaffolded the FastAPI backend inside Docker to satisfy isolation. We ran the Node build script to align the manifests. And we wired P.R. forty-four to GitHub Actions. One hundred and sixty-four canonical checks must pass before the merge button turns green.

beats.narration_text: So what happens if we bypass the gate? A developer adds a local Python package, forgets to freeze requirements dot txt, and forces a push. Without axis three — the C.I. gate — the container builds successfully on their laptop and hard-crashes on the server. The matrix catches that discrepancy before it ships.

beats.narration_text: So don't trust your environment. Audit it. Run the promotion script on your own repository right now. If it returns anything other than zero un-synced manifests, your environment is already drifting.
beats.new_visual_element: The command the viewer runs, and the only passing output

show.event: code card opens on a hard cut; traffic-light dot arms terracotta
the TASK command reveals
the PASS condition reveals beneath it
the failure reading lands last — anything else means drift

props.title: audit.sh
props.code:
# TASK
node scripts/build-instructions.mjs --promote

# PASS
0 un-synced manifests

# ANYTHING ELSE
# your environment is already drifting —
# the manifests on disk and the manifests
# in the repo have diverged, and only one
# of them is what CI will build.

beats.narration_text: And when that audit comes back dirty, here is the prompt worth running. Hand a model your Dockerfile, your requirements file and your CI workflow, and make it score all three against the matrix — then name the single axis you are weakest on. The axis you skip is the one that fails in production.

beats.narration_text: Verification you can trust starts with an environment that cannot drift. Onkar Bhujbal, for Humanitarians AI.
